intervals.label: Forschungszentrum Karlsruhe (predecessor institution on Campus North)

The end is the merger date: "On October 01, 2009 did both institutions merge into the new legal entity of KIT."

name: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Campus North
notes: Campus North is the site of the former Forschungszentrum Karlsruhe (founded 1956 as the Kernreaktor Bau- und Betriebsgesellschaft, later Kernforschungszentrum Karlsruhe); KIT as a legal entity dates from the merger with Universität Karlsruhe on 1 October 2009. The first interval is therefore the predecessor institution's, so that KASCADE (from 1996) and KASCADE-Grande (from 2003), which stood on the Forschungszentrum site before KIT existed, do not predate their host. No source read dates the Tritium Laboratory Karlsruhe itself.
This record covers KIT Campus North (the Tritium Laboratory Karlsruhe site) at the level needed for KATRIN's host-facility role; it is not a full record of KIT as a university/research organisation.

summary.plain: A large German research campus north of Karlsruhe that hosts the Tritium Laboratory Karlsruhe, home to the KATRIN neutrino-mass experiment.
summary.technical: KIT Campus North (Eggenstein-Leopoldshafen, Germany) hosts the Tritium Laboratory Karlsruhe, the site of the KATRIN experiment.
